summary: When the other Kohanim saw that the first Kohen had taken the ashes, they ran up the mizbe'ach too. They moved the leftover pieces of korbanos from the night to the sides.
stIntro: The previous mishna described the performance of the removal of the ashes by the priest who was selected to perform this task. This mishna continues:

chunks.en: His brothers saw that he went down,
chunks.st: The brethren of the priest who removed the ashes, i.e., the other members of the patrilineal family, saw that he had descended from the altar with the coal pan,

chunks.en: and they ran and came (to the kiyor).
chunks.st: and they would run and come to the Basin.

chunks.he: מִהֲרוּ וְקִדְּשׁוּ יְדֵיהֶן וְרַגְלֵיהֶן מִן הַכִּיּוֹר,
chunks.en: They hurried and washed their hands and feet from the kiyor,
chunks.st: They made haste and sanctified their hands and their feet with the water in the Basin, and then

chunks.en: took the shovels and the forks,
chunks.st: they took the shovels

chunks.en: and went up to the top of the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: and the forks and ascended with them to the top of the altar.
chunks.stMore: The shovels were for shoveling the ashes to the center of the altar, while the forks were required to remove from the altar those limbs that had not been consumed.

chunks.en: The pieces of the korbanos and the fats that did not burn up from the night before,
chunks.st: With regard to the limbs of burnt offerings and the fats of other offerings that had not been consumed and burned to ashes during the time from the previous evening, the priests would

chunks.en: they push them to the sides of the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: clear them to the sides of the altar.

chunks.en: If the sides do not have room for them,
chunks.st: If the remaining limbs and fats were so abundant that the sides of the altar were unable to hold them, the priests would

chunks.en: they line them up on the ramp, across from the ledge.
chunks.st: arrange them on the ramp, opposite the surrounding ledge of the altar.

words.note: The sovev, a ledge that goes around the mizbe'ach.

summary: The Kohanim piled the ashes onto a big round heap in the middle of the mizbe'ach. On Yom Tov they left the heap there, because it made the mizbe'ach look beautiful.

chunks.he: הֵחֵלּוּ מַעֲלִין בָּאֵפֶר עַל גַּבֵּי הַתַּפּוּחַ.
chunks.en: They began to bring the ashes up onto the tapuach.
chunks.st: began raising the ashes onto the circular heap upon which the ashes were piled.

words.note: A big round heap of ashes on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: The tapuach was in the middle of the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: The circular heap was in the middle of the altar.

chunks.en: Sometimes there were about three hundred kor of ashes on it.
chunks.st: Sometimes there was as much as three hundred kor of ashes upon it.
chunks.stMore: When the heap of ashes became excessively large, the priests would remove the ashes and pour them outside the city.

chunks.en: On Yom Tov they did not clear it away,
chunks.st: But during the Festivals they would not remove the ashes from the altar,

chunks.en: because it is a beauty for the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: as the ashes were considered an adornment to the altar,
chunks.stMore: since they were a sign of the great number of offerings that were sacrificed on it.

chunks.en: In all its days, the Kohen was never lazy
chunks.st: In all the days of the altar, even when there was an abundance of ashes upon it, the priest tasked with removing the ashes from the circular heap was never indolent

chunks.en: about taking out the ashes.
chunks.st: in removing the ashes.

summary: The Kohanim began to bring up logs to build the fire on the mizbe'ach. Any kind of wood may be used except olive and grapevine, but they usually used fig, nut, and pine wood.
stIntro: After the ashes were cleared to the middle of the altar, the priests

chunks.he: הֵחֵלּוּ מַעֲלִין בְּגִזְרִין לְסַדֵּר אֵשׁ הַמַּעֲרָכָה.
chunks.en: They began to bring up logs to set up the fire on the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: began raising logs onto the altar in order to assemble the arrangement of wood on which the offerings were burned.

words.note: The pile of wood burning on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: Is every kind of wood good for the fire?
chunks.st: The tanna asks: And is wood from all the trees fit for the arrangement?

chunks.en: Yes, every kind of wood is good for the fire,
chunks.st: The tanna replies: Wood from all the trees is fit for the arrangement,

chunks.en: except olive wood and grapevine wood.
chunks.st: except for wood from the vine and from the olive tree,

chunks.en: But they usually used these:
chunks.st: but the priests were accustomed to assemble the arrangement with wood from these trees:

chunks.en: young branches of fig trees, and of
chunks.st: With young branches of the fig tree, of the

chunks.en: nut trees, and of pine trees.
chunks.st: nut tree, and of pinewood.

summary: The Kohen built the big fire on the east side of the mizbe'ach. He left spaces between the logs to light the small sticks.
stIntro: The priest who removed the ashes then

chunks.en: He set up the big ma'arachah on the east side,
chunks.st: assembled the large arrangement of wood upon which the daily offering and the sacrificial portions of the other offerings are burned. It was assembled on the eastern side of the altar,

chunks.en: and its front faced east.
chunks.st: and its opening was on the eastern side of the altar,

chunks.he: וְרָאשֵׁי הַגִּזְרִין הַפְּנִימִיִּם הָיוּ נוֹגְעִים בַּתַּפּוּחַ.
chunks.en: The inside ends of the logs touched the tapuach.
chunks.st: and the inner end of the logs would touch the circular heap of ashes.

chunks.en: There was space between the logs,
chunks.st: And there was space between the logs, in which the priests placed twigs,

chunks.en: because they lit the small sticks from there.
chunks.st: as they would ignite the kindling [ha’alita] from there, so that the fire would spread to the logs.

summary: The Kohanim chose good fig wood to build a second fire, for the ketores. Then they lit both fires and went down to the Lishkas HaGazis.

chunks.en: They picked out nice fig wood from there
chunks.st: selected from among the logs that were there fine logs from fig trees,
chunks.stMore: as when this type of wood was burned it would become coals rather than ashes. The priest who removed the ashes then

chunks.en: to set up a second ma'arachah for the ketores,
chunks.st: assembled the second arrangement of wood, from which the coals were taken to the golden altar in the Sanctuary for the burning of the incense. The second arrangement was assembled

words.note: Incense burned on the golden mizbe'ach inside.

chunks.en: across from the southwest corner,
chunks.st: next to the southwestern corner of the altar and was

chunks.en: stretched out from the corner toward
chunks.st: removed from the corner toward the

chunks.en: the north, four amos.
chunks.st: north side of the altar by a distance of four cubits. The second arrangement was assembled

chunks.en: with enough wood to make five se'ahs of coals.
chunks.st: of an amount of wood estimated to produce five se’a of coals.

words.note: A se'ah is a measure for an amount.

chunks.en: And on Shabbos, with enough to make eight se'ahs of coals,
chunks.st: And on Shabbat, it was assembled of an amount of wood estimated to produce eight se’a of coals,

chunks.en: because there they put the two bowls of
chunks.st: as there the priests would place the two bowls of

chunks.en: levonah of the lechem hapanim.
chunks.st: frankincense that accompanied the shewbread and that were burned on the altar on Shabbat.

words.note: A sweet-smelling spice burned on the mizbe'ach.
The lechem hapanim, the special breads on the Shulchan.

chunks.en: The pieces of the korbanos and the fats that did not burn up from the night before,
chunks.st: With regard to the limbs and the fats that were not consumed during the time from the previous evening, the priests would

chunks.en: they put them back on the big ma'arachah.
chunks.st: return them to the large arrangement to be burned.

chunks.en: They lit the two ma'arachos with fire,
chunks.st: And the priests kindled those two arrangements with fire and

chunks.en: and went down and came to the Lishkas HaGazis.
chunks.st: descended from the altar. And they then came to the Chamber of Hewn Stone,
chunks.stMore: where they would conduct the second lottery in order to determine who would perform the subsequent rites.

words.note: The Lishkas HaGazis, a room of smooth stone where they held the lotteries.
